experience.role: AI Engineer (Agent Orchestration, Memory, RAG & Systems)
highlights: Built the flagship Daily Brief agent (Python/FastAPI) — an agentic orchestration loop over Email, Calendar, and Exa AI web-search tools via asyncio.
Architected a multi-tier memory system (working/medium/long-term) on MongoDB and Redis.

Built an LLM evaluation pipeline with promptfoo benchmarking 8+ models (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Grok, GLM, Kimi, Nemotron) on tool-calling, memory retrieval, latency, and conversation quality; adopted it into the dev cycle.
Cut routing-LLM token usage by 82% via artifact-based prompting and context deduplication — optimized 3 prompts while raising accuracy over the few-shot baseline.
Implemented Langfuse observability for LLM traces, latency, and cost.

Worked on CASA security standards: logout token invalidation via a Redis token_denylists collection (TTL matched to the token's own expiry), email-header injection sanitization, and MongoDB collection-name normalization.
Built voice AI streaming with the Cartesia provider — audio packets with emotion tags and word timestamps, regex-parsed to stay in sync with the text channel.
Parallelized the orchestrator's tool calling, significantly cutting execution time and token usage; added retry semantics so the agentic loop recovers from empty OpenRouter responses and continues.
Implemented live task updates — the main LLM can amend an ongoing task without stopping the Orchestrator's running execution loop.

Shipped the WhatsApp moderation agent: natural-language rule/group management via dedicated agents with their own memory files, a send/delete-message tool, reply-context memory for WhatsApp replies, and a Periskope→WAHA provider migration.
Made task scheduling timezone-correct: moved system time to UTC and handled per-user local timezones, so relative ('in 10 minutes') and absolute ('at 2 pm') reminders execute at the right time.
Added user style adaptation: a storage LLM summarizes each user's talking style per conversation turn into a preferences collection the conversation LLM uses to mirror the user.
Built proactive morning/evening check-ins that run asynchronously over conversation history and medium/long-term memories to surface things the user may have missed.
Built the canvas tool — persistent, per-user websites/docs/PPTs generated by the agentic loop, with data-shape versioning and automatic migration across updates.
Hardened auth: OTP phone verification (hashed OTPs, rate limiting, token expiry) and Apple Sign In; fixed a lost-webhook concurrency bug by moving active working memory into Redis with TTL.
Built the Next.js dashboard for WhatsApp group-rule automation, monitoring, auth routes, and account deletion.
Wrote a project reset script that cut development and testing iteration time by 20%.
Developed CircuitSynth, fine-tuning Qwen 4B/8B with LoRA/QLoRA to generate executable Arduino circuit JSONs.
Achieved 75% accuracy (vs ~0% for base GPT models) via a multi-stage RAG pipeline with automated validation.
Ran quantized GGUF models on Raspberry Pi for edge deployment.
Built a drag-and-drop circuit-diagram dataset tool (Wokwi component library, HTML-element pins with hidden pseudo-pins) and authored a 777-example fine-tuning dataset with multiple review passes.
Tracked fine-tuning runs (temperature, RAM/GPU usage) with Weights & Biases for the research paper.
Shipped the full deployment app — Next.js frontend, FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL, self-built auth — with a side-by-side evaluation UI comparing outputs against OpenAI GPT-5 and Gemini Pro.
Contributed to the project's research paper, copyright, and patent filings.
Built Samagra, a full-stack campus ERP platform grown to 10,000+ active users — React Native mobile client, Node.js/Express REST API, MongoDB, and a Next.js web app.
Engineered JWT auth with role-based access control, rate limiting, and Socket.io real-time sync, sustaining 99.9% uptime.
Owned the product end-to-end — architecture, CI/CD, release, and Play Store distribution — on a zero-cost Vercel-hosted backend handling 150k+ monthly API requests at sub-100ms latency.
Spearheaded development of 6 commercial web applications using the MERN stack, cutting client dev costs by 30% and reducing time-to-market by 45%.
Designed scalable REST APIs and MongoDB schemas supporting 50,000+ monthly requests with 99.9% uptime and sub-100ms response times.
Built high-performance landing pages (HTML5, Tailwind CSS, ES6+) reaching 95+ Google PageSpeed scores and increasing user engagement by 40%.
Integrated CI/CD pipelines and testing workflows, cutting deployment time by 60% while maintaining 98% code coverage.

projects.name: EmailPartner
highlights: Multi-user service turning every new Gmail message into an AI card — headline, summary, illustration, and voice narration — live in a web feed.

Pipeline: Google OIDC consent → AES-GCM envelope-encrypted refresh token → Gmail `users.watch` → Pub/Sub push webhook → `users.history.list` sync → durable worker queue → Gemini summarization, Imagen illustration, and Gemini TTS.
The pending email row IS the job — a lease sweep reclaims stalled work so jobs survive worker restarts.

projects.name: Web-Aware RAG Engine
highlights: Production-style RAG engine: asynchronous web ingestion, semantic search, and cited AI answers.
Nginx round-robins across three FastAPI backend replicas; Next.js 15 / React 19 frontend.

projects.name: voice-sdk
highlights: Unified TypeScript SDK exposing one interface for text-to-speech and speech-to-text across Cartesia, Deepgram, and ElevenLabs, so an application switches providers with a one-line change.
Per-provider capability declarations surface unsupported features up front, with a clear message naming the provider responsible.
The suite runs offline against mock servers, requiring no vendor API keys or spend; a separate live tier validates against real vendors before release. Four packages are versioned together.

projects.name: whoami (Résumé Studio)
highlights: Self-deploying résumé system: a LaTeX source of truth compiled, guarded, and shipped by GitHub Actions on every push.

Quality gates run source structure checks before the expensive compile, then verify the rendered PDF (exactly one page, sections survive extraction, contact email present) and parse LaTeX logs for `Overfull \hbox` overflow.
Vercel serverless function serves the PDF with Redis-backed view counting, content-negotiates HTML+OpenGraph for social crawlers, and still serves the PDF if Redis is down.

Ships a job-search toolkit as a CLI, chat agent, and MCP server (19 tools) for Claude Code / Cursor, with deterministic no-LLM JD scoring and all claims grounded in a hand-verified fact base to prevent fabrication.
